Do you ever feel like you are always behind and can never catch up with the housework? ⁠

Are you overwhelmed by the mess in your house and find it difficult to get it under control? ⁠

If you’re ready to end that cycle, this fall is the time — you belong in Homekeeping Society. ⁠

When I started Clean Mama, all I wanted was to create a simple and natural way to clean my home. I developed a system that worked so well for me that friends and family started using it too. ⁠
⁠
I started a blog and sold homekeeping printables on Etsy. The Clean Mama brand continued to grow, which led to the creation of Homekeeping Society in 2014.
⁠
Between the accountability, resources, and coaching calls, you get everything you need to stay on track even when life gets busy. ⁠
⁠
Save time by knowing exactly what to do and how to KEEP your home clean with Clean Mama’s direction and focus.⁠
⁠
Homekeeping Society is open now through August 13 — join this week and get the Fall Reset Kit free. This is the last time you’ll have to figure it out on your own. Comment SOCIETY for the link!

This might surprise you coming from someone who owns a shop that sells cleaning products…

But I don’t think you need a different cleaner for every room, every surface, or every mess.

In fact, I think that’s part of what makes cleaning feel so overwhelming.

Over the years, I’ve narrowed my routine down to a handful of trusted, multi-purpose products that I use again and again. They work, they’re easy to grab, and I never have to stand in my cleaning closet wondering which bottle to use.

That’s really what the Clean Mama Routine has always been about.

Not buying more or doing more, but making fewer decisions. When you remove the guesswork, it’s so much easier to stay consistent.

A simple routine.
A simple cleaning caddy.

That’s what keeps a home clean.

items.caption:
Have you ever avoided unloading the dishwasher because you “didn’t have time”…
…only to finally do it and realize it took less than three minutes?

Or walked past an unmade bed all morning because it felt like one more thing on your list…
…when it actually took less than a minute?

We tend to overestimate how long everyday tasks take, especially when we’re already feeling overwhelmed.

That’s why I don’t wait until I have a whole afternoon to clean.
I use the little pockets of time I already have.

One small task.
A few minutes.
Done.

Those tiny wins build momentum, and over time they become the routine that keeps your home feeling calm.

I know this one is going to be controversial. 😂

Years ago, I stopped using a top sheet, and honestly…I’ve never looked back.

Here’s why:

✨ It’s one less thing to wash every week.
✨ Making the bed takes less time.
✨ A duvet cover or washable quilt works better for my family and stays in place without the daily sheet battle.

For me, homekeeping is all about finding little ways to make everyday tasks easier.

It’s about creating routines and systems that work for your home.

If you love your top sheet, keep it! If you’ve been thinking about skipping it, this might be your sign to give it a try.

Now let’s settle this once and for all…

👇 Are you Team Top Sheet or Team No Top Sheet?

items.transcript: Another one of my cleaning hot takes is that I don't use a top sheet. This may seem crazy to some, but there are good reasons behind it. First of all, it's one less thing to wash every week, because I do wash sheets on Saturdays. Second, without a top sheet, making the bed is a little faster. I straighten the duvet, fluff the pillows, and I'm done. You can use a duvet cover or a quilt, either one works well, it stays put, it's comfortable, and there's less sheets to untangle. You don't need to necessarily ditch your top sheet, but it is one of those small changes that make homekeeping a little simpler.

items.caption:
I know…this one might surprise some people but if you’ve been following along, I haven’t used it for over 20 years and it’s a big reason why Clean Mama is even here.

Most of the messes we’re cleaning are everyday dirt, dust, fingerprints, grease, soap scum, and spills. Those don’t usually require bleach or harsh chemicals to clean effectively.

Instead, I keep things simple with a few products I use over and over again:
✨ Hydrogen peroxide
✨ Oxygen Whitener ✨ Rubbing alcohol  ✨ Steam ✨ DIY cleaners made with vinegar or vodka ✨ Microfiber cloths

One of the biggest misconceptions about a clean home is that it has to smell like bleach to be clean. 
It doesn’t.
A clean home smells...clean.

The fewer products you own, the fewer decisions you have to make, and the easier it becomes to keep up with your routine. You can also find Clean Mama cleaning products in my shop - they’re simple and they WORK. 

💬 What’s your biggest cleaning must-have? Or is there one product you’ll never give up? Tell me below!

#CleanMama #CleanMamaRoutine #NaturalCleaning #SimpleCleaning CleaningRoutine HealthyHome Homekeeping LowToxLiving CleaningTips CleanHome
items.transcript: I don't use bleach to clean my home. The first reason is I don't think it's necessary for everyday cleaning. We are cleaning grease, dirt, dust, grime, fingerprints. You don't need a harsh chemical to clean those. I just don't think you need a cabinet full of cleaners when a few simple ingredients work just as well. Instead, I reach for simple ingredients like hydrogen peroxide. You can put a spray top on this. This is going to disinfect just as bleach, but you won't have the chemicals in it. I also use steam. I will use rubbing alcohol. Rubbing alcohol is great for high-touch surfaces. You can pour a little bit on a soft cleaning cloth and wipe down light switches and door handles and remove germs just as well as bleach that way. I also like using a steam cleaner. Clean doesn't have to smell like bleach to be clean. It just has to be clean.

items.caption:
Do you have a weekly deep cleaning day? 👀

Here’s one of my biggest cleaning hot takes:

I don’t believe you need one.

If your entire house depends on one big cleaning day each week, missing that day can leave you feeling overwhelmed and behind before the next week even begins.

Instead, I divide my cleaning into simple Daily and Weekly Tasks.

✨ Monday: Bathrooms
✨ Tuesday: Dust
✨ Wednesday: Vacuum
✨ Thursday: Wash Floors
✨ Friday: Catch-All
✨ Saturday: Sheets & Towels
✨ Sunday: Daily Tasks

Each task takes just a little time, but together they keep your home clean all week long—without marathon cleaning sessions or trying to find an entire day to clean.

After more than 20 years of following this routine, I can honestly say I don’t have a “deep cleaning day.”

I have a system.

💬 Do you have a designated cleaning day, or do you spread it out throughout the week?

items.caption:
I haven’t had to decide when to wash my sheets and towels in over 20 years.
That might sound like a small thing, but it’s actually one of the biggest reasons the Clean Mama Routine works.
When you assign a Weekly Task to a specific day, you stop relying on memory, motivation, or guessing.

You don’t have to wonder: Did I wash the sheets last week? How many times have these towels been used?

You already know.
That’s one less decision to make, and one more thing your routine handles for you.
The goal isn’t to create more rules.
It’s to create a simple rhythm that makes caring for your home feel easier.

items.caption:
Friday might be the most important day in the Clean Mama Routine. Not because I clean more, because I finish the week with intention.

Friday is Catch-All Day - it’s the day I take care of the little things that didn’t get done, put things back where they belong, and reset my home before the weekend begins.

That simple habit changes how my weekends feel. Instead of waking up on Saturday already behind, I wake up knowing my home is ready for whatever the weekend brings.

✨That’s what the Clean Mama Routine is all about: creating a simple rhythm that keeps your home manageable and gives you back the time and mental space to enjoy your life.

Thursday is Floor Washing Day...and it’s not because my floors need it.
Most people wait until something looks dirty before they clean it.
I don’t.

By Thursday, the bathrooms are done, the dusting is finished, and the vacuuming is complete. Washing the floors is simply the last step in the Weekly Tasks.

That’s what makes the Clean Mama Routine different.

You’re not reacting to the mess—you’re following a simple rhythm that keeps your home manageable without spending your weekends catching up.

items.caption:
Wednesday is Vacuum Day—and it’s more intentional than you might think.
Vacuuming isn’t just about keeping your floors clean, it’s the next step after Dusting Day.

By dusting on Tuesday and vacuuming on Wednesday, you’re working with your home instead of cleaning the same areas over and over again.
That’s the difference between having a cleaning schedule and having a system.

When the order is already decided, there’s less second-guessing, less overwhelm, and fewer decisions to make.

items.caption:
Dusting Day isn’t just about dust.
The Weekly Tasks aren’t just a checklist—they’re designed to work together.

Tuesday comes before Vacuum Day for a reason. When you dust, everything falls downward. By dusting first and vacuuming the next day, you’re working with your home instead of cleaning the same surfaces twice.

The order isn’t random. It’s intentional.
